Subject: Interest in multi-year step-down commit with performance credits

Hey Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked great for our interactive features. We ran an internal forecast and are evaluating a 2-year prepay with an annual true-up. High-level asks:
- Target effective discount in the 18–22% range (depending on payment timing and SLA credits)

- Want a clear mechanism for performance credits if we hit sub-SLO availability/latency regressions

Hi Sarah — great to hear. Appreciate the forecast.

Quick sketch from our side (initial proposal):
- 2-year annual prepay (invoice at start of each 12-month period)
- Base discount: 20% for 2-year prepay (falls to 18% if customer requests monthly billing or delayed payment terms)
- Step-down protection: quarterly true-up to catch under-usage; unused committed tokens in year N can be credited at 70% value into year N+1 (one-time carryover)
- Performance credits: up to 5% of annual invoice returned as credits if rolling 30-day P99 latency or availability SLO missed; credits applied to next invoice
- Contract mechanics: PO + DocuSign, standard Redwood terms, with a specific SLO appendix for credits

CC'ing Marissa to confirm approval path and finance constraints. If that looks reasonable I can draft a Mutual Action Plan and send to procurement.

Attachments: none in this message.

Thanks for the sketch, Jonas — good starting point. Internals:
- Finance: we need to protect gross margin; recommend we hold discount to a 20% list-price reduction for two-year prepay with the conditions listed below.
- Sales ops: require a clear escalator clause if Cloudwise wants month-to-month carry or delayed invoicing — that should reduce the effective discount by 2pp.

Counter-proposal to present to Cloudwise (attach to MAP):
1) 2-year annual prepay (invoiced Year 1 & Year 2 at signature) — 20% off list on prepay schedule
2) Step-down/Carry rules: quarterly true-ups; unconsumed committed units can be carried forward to the next quarter at 70% credit; any leftover at end of Year 2 converted to one-time credit at 50%
3) Performance credits: up to 5% of the annual invoice if availability < 99.5% for a rolling 30-day window; for latency regressions apply tiered credits tied to P95/P99 miss thresholds
4) Early termination: standard pro-rata refund rules with clawback on discounts if Cloudwise terminates early for convenience

Attached: proposed_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (outlines discount bands and sample calculations). Markus, Ben — please flag any blockers; if finance signs off we can accept 20% and ask procurement for PO + signature within 10 business days.

—Marissa

Marissa/Jonas — reviewed the numbers with finance modelling.

Takeaways:
- 20% on a pure prepay is tight but acceptable if we get annual pre-invoice and no extended payment terms beyond Net 30.
- If procurement asks for Net 60 or PO-based delayed payment we should reduce to 18% (floor).
- The step-down carry mechanics are reasonable; make sure the contract limits carry to 2 quarters (to avoid perpetual credits).
- Approve one-time up-to-2% accelerator (extra discount) if Cloudwise commits to a modest growth ramp (15% YoY) and provides usage telemetry integration within 60 days.

I've attached a short pricing_calculator_CW-112.xlsx with margin impact scenarios. If Marissa wants to proceed, finance is comfortable with 20% conditioned on PO terms and signature timing.
